Subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — BlueHarbor Analytics

Hi Sam / Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation last week — great alignment on latency targets and the 24/7 inference window. Attached is a first-pass proposal with three reservation options tailored to the BlueHarbor forecast you shared: conservative, balanced, and growth. Each option includes: cluster size, minimum guaranteed GPUs, a 12‑week ramp schedule, burst lanes for headroom, and estimated monthly unit costs.

High level (summary):
- Conservative: 8 min GPUs guaranteed, target steady-state 16 GPUs by week 12. Lower monthly commit, higher overage risk on peak.
- Balanced: 16 min GPUs guaranteed, target steady-state 32 GPUs by week 12. Best blend for predicted traffic.
- Growth: 32 min GPUs guaranteed, target steady-state 64 GPUs by week 12 with priority burst lanes and 99.9% latency SLO.

Notes and asks:
- We included two ramp profiles — linear and "stair-step" (3 tranches). See tab "RampProfiles" in the attached cluster_sizing_model.xlsx.
- Pricing in the PDF shows per-GPU committed rate and expected overage/spot rates. If procurement needs an annual commit we can provide a discount schedule (outlined page 3).
- Please confirm which option (or a hybrid) you want Priya to convert into a formal SOW + DocuSign route.

Attachments: [blueharbor_proposal_v1.pdf] [cluster_sizing_model.xlsx]

Best,
Priya Natarajan

From: Sam Park <sam.park@blueharbor.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — BlueHarbor Analytics

Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. A few clarifying items from our side before we loop procurement: 

1) Minimum guaranteed GPUs: Procurement will insist on a minimum guarantee but also needs flexibility — can you show a lower guaranteed floor for the first 6 months that transitions to the Balanced option at month 7?
2) Ramp cadence: Our product team prefers stair-step (tranches) but with smaller first tranche — can you make the first tranche 4 weeks instead of 6?
3) Burst lanes and preemption: If we use burst capacity during the morning peak, how does that affect latency SLOs and billing reconciliation?
4) Compliance: Elena will need SOC2 evidence and the location of audit logs for our security review.

Also looped procurement: procurement@blueharbor.ai — they will want a clear table of monthly committed spend vs overage estimates and an outline of onboarding timeline (SLA activation, provisioning lead times).

If you can update the proposal with: (a) a 6‑month lowered guarantee path, (b) 4‑week first tranche stair-step, (c) explicit burst billing example, and (d) a link to SOC2 evidence, we can aim to review with procurement next week.

Cheers,
Sam
Director of ML Platform | BlueHarbor Analytics
sam.park@blueharbor.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — BlueHarbor Analytics

Priya — looping in engineering notes for an updated attachment and numbers.

We can support the requested variation (6‑month lowered floor -> transition) with these recommendations: 
- Option A (phased floor): Months 0–6 guarantee 8 GPUs, months 7–12 move to 16 GPUs guaranteed, target steady-state 32 by week 12 post-transition.
- Stair-step ramp (adjusted): Tranche 1 = 4 weeks (8->12 GPUs), Tranche 2 = next 4 weeks (12->20), Tranche 3 = final 4 weeks (20->32). This smooths cold cache costs and KV warming.
- Burst lanes: recommend soft-burst (elastic spot-backed) for peak; we carve burst at +25% capacity with billing at an overage multiplier. In practical terms: if baseline commit is 16 GPUs, burst up to 20 GPUs billed at 1.5x for the bursted units. This preserves 99th pctl latency for committed units and gives headroom for short peaks.
- Latency SLO impact: committed capacity retains SLO; requests served on burst lanes have best-effort latency target (documented in SLA scenarios).

Attached: sla_scenarios.csv with sample latency vs cost tradeoffs and a revised cluster_sizing_model tab. If procurement needs a month-by-month spend table I can produce a burn-rate CSV with the same inputs.

[Attachment: sla_scenarios.csv]

Ben / Lauren — any commercial language we should preempt for the SOW (credits, ramp breakpoints)?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.narian@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — BlueHarbor Analytics

Sam / Elena / procurement team — attaching an updated one‑pager and the revised sizing workbook reflecting the 6‑month floor + 4‑week first tranche stair-step. Key changes summarized below: 

- Phased floor path: Months 0–6 guaranteed = 8 GPUs, months 7–12 guaranteed = 16 GPUs, projected steady-state = 32 GPUs by week 12 post-transition.
- Ramp: 3 tranches (4 / 4 / 4 weeks) with KV pre-warming notes.
- Burst pricing example: +25% burst capacity billed at 1.5x for bursted capacity; included a sample monthly invoice line for the expected morning peak.
- Compliance: SOC2 report link: https://drive.google.com/blueharbor-soc2 (read-only). Audit logs are retained for 13 months by default; we can extend per contract.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Procurement: confirm whether you prefer a 12‑month or 24‑month committed term (discounts outlined in page 3 of the attached PDF).
2) Once term is chosen, I will convert to an SOW with commercial language and a DocuSign link.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/preview/BH-2026-482 (will be active after procurement confirms term).

Attachments sent: [blueharbor_proposal_v1.pdf] [cluster_sizing_model.xlsx] [sla_scenarios.csv]

Looking forward — happy to set a 30‑minute call with procurement if that helps move the SOW.
